rounds.text: Pasupati Spinning & Weaving Mills Ltd trades at an exceptionally low P/E of 7.68x against a sector benchmark of 14.76x, alongside a price-to-book ratio of 0.95x that sits below its sector benchmark of 1.21x [E1, E6, E7]. This statistical cheapness masks a profound fundamental disconnect, as a discounted cash flow analysis places intrinsic value at Rs 174 per share, leaving a margin of safety of 78.9% while the current market price only discounts a negative 3.6% growth rate [E43, E44, E45]. Profitability metrics are rapidly expanding and outperforming peers, highlighted by an ROA of 4.14% and ROE of 12.39% that comfortably exceed sector benchmarks, alongside an operating margin that has widened by 6 percentage points over three years to 11% [E8, E9, E30]. Cash generation is exceptionally robust with a 2.50x cash conversion ratio for March 2026, translating to Rs 5 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 3 Cr in free cash flow, proving that recent earnings growth of 286% in the trailing twelve months is fully backed by real cash [E21, E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, fundamentals are drastically outpacing stock price movement, with 5-year profit growth of 19% easily eclipsing 13% price growth, supported by a favorable textile sector tailwind score of +0.53 [E19, E23, E46, E60]. Conceded: debt to equity stands at 1.42x with borrowings flat at Rs 51 Cr, and the company currently pays a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E37, E38].

Despite surface-level cheapness, Pasupati Spinning & Weaving Mills Ltd carries severe structural weaknesses, highlighted by a concerning debt-to-equity ratio of 1.42x where total borrowings of Rs 51 Cr exceed the company's net worth [E37, E38]. Long-term top-line expansion has actually contracted, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -6% and a 3-year compounded sales growth of -10% [E14, E16], accompanied by poor 5-year sales growth of 8.38% [E51]. Profitability metrics remain lackluster over any meaningful timeframe, underlined by a dismal 10-year median return on equity of 0% [E26], a 5-year median ROE of just 4% [E27], and a low 3-year average ROE of 4.89% [E52]. Furthermore, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% despite reporting repeated profits, withholding any cash return to shareholders [E4, E50]. Conceded: [E21].

While the bear points to high leverage, total borrowings have remained completely flat at Rs 51 Cr year-over-year [E38], while cash generation has surged to cover obligations with Rs 5 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 3 Cr in free cash flow for Mar 2026 [E35, E36]. On top-line contraction, the bear ignores that sales are growing at 9% over the trailing twelve months alongside a recent quarterly jump of 17% YoY [E17, E54]. The criticism of historically weak ROE overlooks that current profitability is outperforming benchmarks, with an ROE of 12.39% beating the sector's 7.21% and an operating margin expanding to 11% [E8, E9, E30]. Conceded: [E4, E50]. Furthermore, the company's profit growth has vastly outpaced its share price gains, backed by a staggering 286% surge in TTM profit growth and a sector tailwind score of +0.53 [E21, E46, E60].

Conceded: [E38], [E17], [E54]. While borrowings held flat at Rs 51 Cr, a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.42x means total obligations still exceed the company's net worth, maintaining a clear structural leverage risk [E37]. The cited TTM sales growth and recent quarterly jump do not erase a long-term pattern of top-line contraction, which includes a 10-year compounded sales growth of -6% and a 3-year compounded decline of -10% [E14, E16]. Furthermore, pointing to a single year's high ROE ignores the chronic weakness of historical returns, highlighted by a 10-year median ROE of 0%, a 5-year median of 4%, and a 3-year average as low as 4.89% [E26, E27, E52]. The screen itself flags that earnings growth is actively decelerating alongside low multi-year profitability [E58, E59]. Finally, despite reported profit surges, the complete absence of any dividend payout underscores lingering uncertainties regarding actual shareholder value realization [E4, E50].
